hook.text: A Microsoft study claimed human attention spans dropped to 8 seconds—less than a goldfish. Headlines exploded.

buildup.text: The stat went viral. TED talks cited it. Marketing firms built strategies around it. It felt true.

discovery.text: But the study never said that. The goldfish comparison was invented by media. The data was misread.

twist.text: Humans binge 10-hour Netflix series. Attention hasn't shrunk—it's been redirected to what hooks us best.

climax.text: The myth served platforms well. 'You can't focus' justifies short content. It's a self-fulfilling prophecy.

punchline.text: Your attention span is fine. The competition for it isn't.

quiz.question: What was wrong with the 'goldfish attention span' claim?
options: It was misreported from the data
